purpose: Adds PreconditionerProof/PhaseCorrected.lean (phase-corrected monotonicity) and PreconditionerProof/T1Dimension.lean (optimal policy class is one-dimensional)

headline_result.hypotheses: Nondecreasing n, FirstTrigger rho n K
headline_result.conclusion: (length 0 = K or length 0 = K + 1) and for all t, length (t+1) = K
headline_result.note: DiscreteConvexFromOne appears nowhere in Conservative.lean except the docstring. Compare Online.stationary_policy_correct, which requires it.

changed_in_this_addition: PreconditionerProof/Audit.lean (now imports Conservative and prints its headline theorems)
scope: Stationary noiseless abstract policy with exact fixed rebuild cost and persistent exact age-prefix observations. Conservative predictor replaces an unobserved age by the largest known age; this is an idealization, not a claim that the deployed predictor uses it. Does not model non-stationarity, noisy estimation, phase coupling, or production-code equivalence.
caveats: Paper sources are unchanged: neither PhaseCorrected nor T1 has been written into the manuscript yet.
T1 slack cannot be tightened without restricting to schedules that rebuild at step 0; schedule_lower_bound_exact covers that case.
PhaseCorrected assumes the additive model N(t,a,j)=mu(t)+g(a)+q(j) with exact arithmetic. Additivity is measured separately, not proved.
The statement 'conservative extrapolation never rebuilds early' was retracted on 2026-10-28 after C4 data showed dmed<delta in 76/144 cases; no Lean theorem supports it.

headline_results.statement: additive model + g nondecreasing => phase-corrected curve is nondecreasing within each phase
headline_results.note: mu(t) and q_j cancel in within-phase age differences; a constant offset error only shifts the level

headline_results.statement: with per-observation noise bounded by eps, monotone up to 2*eps
headline_results.note: eps is measurable; this is the 'monotone to the noise floor' statement

headline_results.statement: if the true offset drifts down with age by more than g rises, the corrected curve can fall
headline_results.note: identifies the exact failure channel, motivating the frozen-offset mechanism

headline_results.statement: every schedule costs at least T*c(K*) - rho, uniformly in T
headline_results.note: the slack is rho, not zero: a schedule that delays its first rebuild never pays it

headline_results.statement: q cycles of length K cost exactly (q*K)*c(K)
headline_results.note: so inf over policies = min over fixed periods, up to one rebuild charge

headline_results.statement: the largest minimizer over {1..N} is nondecreasing in rho
headline_results.note: depends on the largest-minimizer convention; on a plateau the smallest-index convention would break monotonicity

headline_results.statement: N(t,a)-N(t,b)=g(a)-g(b): baseline drift cancels exactly in within-time age differences, for drift of arbitrary magnitude
headline_results.note: the claim that this explains the 1.2-6.5% learning cost is NOT supported by the traces and was withdrawn

headline_results.statement: explore one cycle of length Kbar, then q cycles of K*: regret = Kbar*(c(Kbar)-c(K*)), independent of q and hence of T
headline_results.note: requires no monotonicity, convexity or noise assumption; the K* used is the minimiser over 1..Kbar only

headline_results.statement: empirical near-optimality within eps implies true 4*eps near-optimality, with eps = eps_a(n) + eps_d
headline_results.note: interval statements for every realisation, no probability model; eps_d is floored and cannot be reduced by sampling

headline_results.statement: two curves agreeing on the observed prefix 0..m but with different optimal periods cannot both be identified by a prefix-only policy
headline_results.note: identification lower bound, not a cost lower bound; a cost-form bound would need a metric on the class and is not attempted
